author: isabella-janssen
body:
**- What I did**

_Part 1 - Test hardening:_
This hardens the MCN condition transition tests for ImageModeStatusReporting. On rare occasions, such as [this example payload run](https://prow.ci.openshift.org/view/gs/test-platform-results/logs/periodic-ci-openshift-machine-config-operator-release-4.22-periodics-e2e-aws-mco-disruptive-techpreview-1of3/2037173271597682688), we would see the test fail because we never detected the `RebootedNode` condition in a state of `True`. The reboot condition transitions from False --> Unknown --> True --> False, and some stages of the transition can occur quickly. If the reboot were to fail, the condition would stay in `Unknown`, as that is the error condition status, so warning instead of erroring when we miss the `True` condition will not hide true functional errors.

_Part 2 - Modifications for SNO:_
This updates the three ImageModeStatusReporting tests that were designed to run in custom MCPs to run against the master MCP when the worker pool has no nodes. This allows the tests to run in the SNO topology with https://github.com/openshift/release/pull/77273.

**- How to verify it**

_Part 1 - Test hardening:_
I have not been able to reproduce the error and the flake is quite rare, so the best way to verify the fix is likely to run lots of jobs and make sure the flake never appears.

_Part 2 - Modifications for SNO:_
These tests can be verified locally by running them against a SNO cluster or by rehearsing them with https://github.com/openshift/release/pull/77273 once this work merges.

**- Description for the changelog**
NO-JIRA: Harden MCN condition transition tests and adjust tests to run on SNO

body:
`Span::styled_graphemes` internally filters out control characters (including `\n`), which forced a special-case workaround when building the grapheme-index-to-tag map for newline tokens.

## Changes

- **`app/mod.rs`** — Remove the `if/else` newline special-case entirely. `.graphemes(true)` yields `"\n"` as a grapheme, so the tag map is built uniformly for all tokens:
  ```rust
  // Before: if/else with manual vec![Tag::Command(start)] for newlines
  let graph_idx_to_tag: Vec<Tag> = part
      .normal_span()
      .content
      .graphemes(true)
      .scan(part.token.token.byte_range().start, |acc, graph| {
          let tag = Tag::Command(*acc);
          *acc += graph.len();
          Some(tag)
      })
      .collect();
  ```

- **`active_suggestions.rs`** — Replace `span.styled_graphemes(span.style)` with `span.content.graphemes(true)`; style was sourced from `span.style` directly anyway. Adds `use unicode_segmentation::UnicodeSegmentation`.

- **`content_builder.rs`** — Replace `span.styled_graphemes(span.style)` with `.graphemes(true)` and construct `StyledGrapheme { symbol: g, style: span.style }` manually where the style is still needed for cell rendering.

## Summary
This PR adds automated Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) generation and upload to DependencyTrack, enabling better dependency tracking and vulnerability management.

## Key Changes
- **New GitHub Actions Workflow**: Added `.github/workflows/dependency-track.yml` that:
  - Triggers on pushes to main and release publications
  - Generates CycloneDX SBOM in JSON format using `@cyclonedx/cyclonedx-npm`
  - Uploads SBOM to DependencyTrack API with versioning (release tag or nightly build)
  - Uses environment variables and secrets for API configuration

- **Package.json**: Added `sbom:generate` npm script for local SBOM generation

- **.gitignore**: Added `bom.json` to prevent committing generated SBOM files

## Implementation Details
- Version determination: Uses release tag for published releases, or `nightly-{SHORT_SHA}` for main branch pushes
- DependencyTrack integration: Configured with API key and URL via GitHub secrets/variables
- Auto-create project: Enabled in DependencyTrack to automatically create project if it doesn't exist
- Reuses existing setup action for consistent environment configuration

### Motivation

- Improve live-streaming workflows and stability for browser publishing by hardening prepare/publish flows, adding diagnostics, and masking sensitive ICE data.
- Surface clearer live-state presentation and enable a dedicated personal sessions route (`/live/mine`) so creators can manage their own broadcasts.
- Expand internationalization and translate many UI strings for login/register/live flows and category labels.
- Polish UI details across video cards, layout, and live room sidebar for a more consistent and accessible experience.

### Description

- Routing and layout: added a new route `/live/mine`, adjusted menu selected key resolution via `resolveMenuSelectedPath`, and added a language selector dropdown in the top-right utility bar with `menuProps.selectedKeys` support.
- Live create/publish: major refactor in `src/pages/Live/Create` including `prepare` request deduping/locking (`startFlowLockRef`, `prepareRequestInFlightRef`), improved preflight checks, secure URL upgrades, masked ICE server logging (`maskIceServers`), safer WebRTC adaptor load/initialization, structured callback/error handling, diagnostic logging flags and a debug panel toggle.
- Live status & presentation: added `src/utils/liveStatusPresentation.ts` to normalize live UI status and return label/description/color; `Live` and `LiveRoom` pages use the new presentation helpers and improved watch URL canonicalization.
- Category i18n: moved category canonicalization and localized label lookup into a new `src/utils/categoryI18n.ts` and wired it into `Home`, `LiveRoom`, and other pages to display localized category names.
- Video card & UI tweaks: `src/components/VideoCard` receives improved status label sourcing (`status_label`/`status_description`), adjusted colours, hover transitions, spacing, and layout to match updated design.
- Live room sidebar and UX: reworked `LiveRoom` sidebar into a collapsible panel with QR, pay/watch copy actions, chat placeholder area, localized strings, and layout tweaks (avatar/title arrangement).
- i18n additions: expanded `en-US`, `zh-CN`, `th-TH`, and `my-MM` locale files with many new keys for auth, live creation, debug messages, and UI copy; wired translations into `Login`, `Register`, `LiveCreate`, `LiveRoom`, and other pages.

author: gtmacdonald
body:
## Summary

Every GDExtension ptrcall to a method returning `Ref<T>` (any `RefCounted` class) leaks one reference. The engine's `PtrToArg<Ref<T>>::encode` increments the refcount when writing the return value, expecting the caller to absorb the owned reference. godot-cpp handles this with `_gde_internal_constructor`. gdzig reads the raw `Object*` pointer without unreferencing, permanently leaking one reference per call.

This affects all ptrcall returns of RefCounted objects: `get_mesh()`, `get_material()`, `get_texture()`, `get_shader()`, etc.

## Symptoms

- `ERROR: N RID allocations of type 'Mesh' were leaked at exit`
- `ObjectDB instances leaked at exit`
- ArrayMesh, Material, Shader, Texture objects never freed despite correct application code

## Root Cause

In Godot's `core/variant/method_ptrcall.h`, `PtrToArg<Ref<T>>::encode` treats the return buffer as a `Ref<T>` and calls `Ref::operator=`, which increments the refcount. godot-cpp compensates with `_gde_internal_constructor` (sets pointer without calling `reference()`). gdzig has no equivalent — it reads the raw pointer and returns it, leaving the extra reference permanently.

## Fix

In `codegen.zig`, for generated class methods that return a RefCounted type, emit an `unreference()` ptrcall after the method ptrcall to drop the owned reference. A shared `_ref_unreference_mb` method bind pointer is cached per class to avoid repeated lookups.

The caller receives a borrowed pointer — matching GDScript semantics.

## Verification

Tested with a reproduction scene creating 100 `ArrayMesh` instances per cycle across 3 destroy/recreate cycles:
- **Before fix:** 400 leaked Mesh RIDs + ObjectDB leaks
- **After fix:** Zero leaks

Also verified with a full tile rendering system (~3,452 dynamically created meshes with visual mode cycling) — all leaks eliminated.

## Related

- godot-rust/gdext#108 — same issue in godot-rust
- godotengine/godot#73577, #80140, #69910 — RID leak reports partially caused by this

author: debuggerone
body:
Title:
Bound object-store metadata cache growth

Description:
This PR hardens the object-store runtime against memory-growth DoS caused by an unbounded process-local metadata cache.

Included:
- a hard cap for runtime metadata-cache entries
- actual TTL-based eviction instead of unbounded accumulation
- on-demand metadata reload after eviction from sidecar metadata
- runtime/system status surfaces for cache size, cap, and eviction count
- regression coverage for both entry-cap and TTL behavior

Impact:
- prevents unbounded memory growth in long-lived runtimes
- keeps the metadata cache useful without turning it into a process-wide memory sink

author: jin-2-kakaoent
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1101.

The idle `Sleep` future was recreated **inside** the `select!` loop on every iteration. On Unix/macOS, the 500 ms drain interval caused the future to be dropped and replaced before it could reach its deadline. On Windows, incoming connections (`accept`) caused the same timer reset. The daemon never shut down via idle timeout on either platform.

Moved the pinned `Sleep` future **outside** the loop so it survives loop restarts and only resets on actual command receipt (`reset_rx`). Applied the fix to both Unix and Windows `run_socket_server` implementations. Added a cross-platform regression test.

## Reproduction

```bash
AGENT_BROWSER_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS=3000 agent-browser --session repro-timeout open about:blank
sleep 5
agent-browser session list
# Session still alive after 5s (expected: closed after ~3s)
```

## AS-IS (bug)

```
loop start
  └─ create new Sleep future (deadline = now + timeout)
       └─ tokio::select!
            ├─ drain tick (500ms) ← always wins
            │     └─ loop restart → Sleep future dropped
            │           └─ create new Sleep (deadline reset to now + timeout)
            │                 └─ drain tick wins again → drop → create → repeat forever
            │
            └─ idle timeout ← never reached
```

## TO-BE (fix)

```
create Sleep future outside loop + pin
  └─ loop start
       └─ tokio::select!
            ├─ drain tick (500ms)
            │     └─ loop restart, but Sleep is an outer variable → preserved
            │           └─ next select polls same Sleep (500ms remaining)
            │
            ├─ idle timeout (1000ms) ← fires normally → break → daemon exits
            │
            └─ reset_rx (command received)
                  └─ only here: create new Sleep (timer reset)
```

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo check` passes
- [x] `cargo fmt` / `cargo clippy` clean
- [x] `cargo test` — 569 passed, 0 failed
- [x] Manual repro: `AGENT_BROWSER_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS=3000` session now closes after ~3 s of inactivity

💡 **What**
Added explicit `id` and `htmlFor` attributes to associate form labels with their corresponding inputs (`<input>`, `<select>`, and `<textarea>`) in the `CreateChallengeModal`. Also added the `cursor-pointer` Tailwind class to the labels.

Previously, the form elements inside the "Create Challenge" modal lacked explicit label associations. This made the form less accessible for screen reader users and prevented users from clicking the labels to focus the corresponding input fields, which is a common and expected UX pattern.

📸 **Before/After**
*Before*: Clicking "Challenge Identity", "Timeline Duration", or "Strategic Objective" did nothing.
*After*: Clicking any of those labels now correctly focuses the associated input, select, or textarea field.

♿ **Accessibility**
Screen readers can now correctly announce the purpose of each form field because the `<label>` elements are semantically linked to their controls via the `htmlFor` attribute. Keyboard and mouse users also benefit from the increased clickable area.

body:
### Motivation
- Single-shot receive runs could finish without an explicit `--output-file` in the subprocess args, leaving `result["output_file"]` unset and making post-processing/plotting and diagnostics brittle. 
- The UI needs a reliable, testable output path for single-mode RX runs so plots and callers always have a usable file to work with.

### Description
- When `_run_rx_thread()` finds no `--output-file` in `arg_list`, it now generates a timestamped path under `signals/rx` via a new helper ` _make_auto_rx_output_file_path()` and injects `--output-file <path>` into `arg_list` before launching the subprocess. 
- `result["output_file"]` is always populated with the resolved path for single RX runs so downstream code and callers can rely on it. 
- Added an informational log line on single-mode completion containing `ok`, `error` and `output_file` to simplify regression diagnosis. 
- Added a regression test `test_run_rx_thread_single_without_explicit_output_file_sets_result_output_file` that exercises a single RX invocation without `--output-file` and asserts the result contains a usable auto-generated path and that the subprocess args were updated accordingly.

author: georges-gnm
body:
Reverts guardian/tagmanager#627 and should fix the issue seen in prod. The second commit in this PR contains the fix. 

Although I'd tested the original PR in code and it seemed to be working as intended, in prod relevant stream updates weren't coming through. We can confirm this by looking at the logs:
- a tag (local elections 2026) created prior to the original PR getting released provides [these logs](https://logs.gutools.co.uk/s/editorial-tools/app/r/s/noBAr)
- a tag (april fools day) created after shows [these](https://logs.gutools.co.uk/s/editorial-tools/app/r/s/mHeVS).

The salient difference is that the `TagEvent received` message never appears in the latter, and on double checking, weren't coming through when the branch was up on code either ([searching](https://logs.gutools.co.uk/app/r/s/8YnPO) for it in the past couple of weeks only brings up records from today). 

## What's changed

To be transparent, I used Copilot to help investigate this, and it pointed to an issue in the ByteBuffer handling inside KinesisRecordPayloadConversions.

When consuming Kinesis records via the updated KCL client, KinesisClientRecord.data() can return ByteBuffer instances with a non-zero arrayOffset or position, due to KCL's internal pooled/sliced buffer allocation. The previous implementation didn't account for this - it passed the buffer directly without respecting its current position, which meant Thrift could be decoding from the wrong byte index, causing deserialization failures.

The fix updates kinesisRecordAsThriftCompactProtocol to correctly extract the relevant bytes from the ByteBuffer by respecting its position and arrayOffset, so the correct slice of the backing array is always read regardless of how the buffer was constructed.

Additional tests have been added to TagEventDeserialiserTest covering the three ByteBuffer states KCL v2 can produce: clean, sliced (arrayOffset > 0), and positioned (position > 0).

## Testing

Deployed to CODE, I created a new tag (gl-test-kinesis) and in quick succession updated it a few times. These updates came through correctly, and we can see the `TagEvent received` messages in the [logs](https://logs.gutools.co.uk/app/r/s/OqVXn). Considering the level of usage of the code environment vs prod, it feels like there's a limit to how well this can be tested, but those logs give me reassurance that the kinesis stream logic is now correct.

author: titouanmathis
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes a race condition in the deployment command and adds real-time log streaming.

### Fix: Deployment race condition

The deploy command was failing because it polled `/deployments/status` immediately after triggering a deployment. Since the deployment hadn't started yet, the endpoint returned 404, which was incorrectly treated as "deployment done".

**Solution:**
- Capture the deployment ID from the POST response (which returns the created deployment resource)
- Poll the specific deployment by ID (`/deployments/{id}`) instead of the generic status endpoint
- Check for terminal statuses (`finished`, `failed`, `failed-build`) to know when polling is complete

### Feature: `--stream` flag

New `--stream` flag for `forge deployments deploy` that streams logs in real-time:

- **Default mode**: Shows progress status with elapsed time
  ```
  Deploying… deploying (12.5s)
  ```
- **Stream mode**: Streams deployment logs to stdout as they arrive
  ```
  forge deployments deploy --server X --site Y --stream
  ```

The two modes are mutually exclusive to avoid output conflicts.

Closes #84

body:
### Motivation
- Add an automated periodic watcher to disconnect already-connected OpenVPN sessions that move outside their allowed schedules and ensure cron lifecycle is managed by the package.
- Improve robustness of the runtime auth hook to better extract usernames and to use the platform schedule engine when available.

### Description
- Introduces a cron watcher: new `files/usr/local/pkg/openvpn_schedule_cron.php` and cron orchestration in `openvpn_schedule.inc` to install/remove a 5-minute cron job using `OVPN_SCHEDULE_CRON_COMMAND` when any user has a non-`None` schedule. 
- Implements connected-session discovery and disconnection helpers in `openvpn_schedule.inc`, including parsing status files, querying management sockets, and issuing `kill` commands to OpenVPN server sockets.
- Hardens the auth hook in `openvpn_schedule_hook.inc` with case-insensitive username matching, a resilient username extraction routine (from request/env or argv files), schedule lookup that tolerates missing schedules, and delegation to core schedule APIs when present (`filter_schedule_in_effect` / `is_schedule_in_time`).
- Adds cleanup that force-removes stale cron entries during deinstall and when disabling the watcher, and logs actions via `openvpn_schedule_log`.
- Packaging updates: bumped `PORTREVISION`, included `openvpn_schedule_cron.php` in the `Makefile` and `pkg-plist`, and updated documentation `README.md` to describe the periodic disconnect watcher and its behavior.
- Minor UI tweak: use `openvpn_schedule_user_label()` to display user labels with an icon and description in `openvpn_schedule.php`.

### Testing
- Performed PHP syntax checks (`php -l`) on modified PHP files and they reported no syntax errors.
- No automated unit tests were added to this change.

author: jshobe-inetsoft
body:
## Summary

When a logical model is moved to a different folder in the EM, scheduled task backup actions that reference that model were not updated with the new path.

**Root cause**: `RepositoryObjectService.moveDataModel()` builds the `RenameInfo` paths using `/` separators (`database/folder/name`), but `TaskAssetDependencyTransformer.renameBackUpAction()` passed those paths directly to the XAsset XPath lookup, which expects the backup action ID format (`database^__^folder^name`). The path never matched, so the XAsset element was never updated.

**Fix**: Added `toModelAssetPath()` in `TaskAssetDependencyTransformer` to convert `/`-separated paths to the `^__^`/`^` ID format before the lookup. Paths already in ID format (e.g. from `DatabaseModelBrowserService`) contain `^` and are passed through unchanged.

## Test plan

- [ ] Import the attached ZIP from issue #74430 (adds logical model "Order Model" under "F1" folder in "Examples/Orders" data source, plus schedule task "task1" with a backup action referencing it)
- [ ] Drag "Order Model" from "Data Source/Examples/Data Model/F1" to the parent "Data Model" folder
- [ ] Open "task1" in the schedule tab → action tab
- [ ] Verify the asset ID now reflects the new path (no longer contains "F1")

### Motivation
- Reduce runtime footprint and complexity so the image can be used for high-density deployments (hundreds/thousands of containers). 
- Remove optional features and background daemons that are not required for keeping the tunnel up to save memory/cpu. 
- Consolidate reconnection logic into the Docker healthcheck so failure detection and immediate reconnects are done in a single lightweight script.

### Description
- Simplified the Dockerfile to only copy `files/start.sh` and `files/healthcheck.sh`, removed the microsocks build stage and many optional runtime dependencies, and tightened the `HEALTHCHECK` cadence. 
- Rewrote `files/start.sh` to a minimal bootstrap that restores resolver state, starts the ExpressVPN service, activates with `CODE`, sets `PROTOCOL`, connects to `SERVER`, enables background mode, and then `sleep`s indefinitely. 
- Replaced complex multi-feature supervision with a single `files/healthcheck.sh` that verifies `expressvpnctl status` and `tun0`, and attempts an immediate reconnect using `expressvpnctl connect` waiting up to `HEALTHCHECK_RECONNECT_WAIT` seconds for success. 
- Updated `README.md` to document the minimal behavior and list removed features (metrics, control API, SOCKS5, DNS helpers) and runtime env vars for the slim image.

author: mmrajput
body:
## Root cause

`databases-netpol` had an **ingress** rule allowing intra-namespace port 5432 traffic (so the primary accepts replica connections), but **no matching egress rule**. Calico evaluates NetworkPolicy in both directions — the standby join pod's outbound connection to the primary was silently dropped.

Symptom: `nextcloud-prod-db-2-join` pod looping on:
```
DB not available, will retry — dial error: timeout: context deadline exceeded
```

## Fix

Added a single egress rule mirroring the existing ingress rule:

```yaml
# Allow intra-namespace egress (CNPG streaming replication — replica → primary)
- to:
    - podSelector: {}
  ports:
    - port: 5432
      protocol: TCP
```

## Test plan

- [x] ArgoCD syncs `databases-netpol` — verify with `kubectl get networkpolicy -n databases`
- [x] `nextcloud-prod-db-2` pod reaches `Running` state (no longer stuck in join loop)
- [x] `kubectl get cluster nextcloud-prod-db -n databases` shows `READY: 2` and `STATUS: Cluster in healthy state`
- [x] Nextcloud production still responds

author: dcaugher
body:
### Description of PR

Summary:
Add `sonic_yang` error pattern to loganalyzer ignore list for `test_multiasic_addcluster` test to prevent false test failures from expected transient YANG validation errors.

Fixes # N/A (test reliability improvement)

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] Testbed and Framework(new/improvement)
- [ ] New Test case
    - [ ] Skipped for non-supported platforms
- [x] Test case improvement


### Back port request
- [ ] 202205
- [ ] 202305
- [ ] 202311
- [ ] 202405
- [ ] 202411
- [ ] 202505
- [ ] 202511

### Approach
#### What is the motivation for this PR?

The `test_multiasic_addcluster` test was failing due to `sonic_yang` YANG validation errors being caught by the loganalyzer. These errors are **expected transient failures** that occur during GCU (Generic Config Updater) patch application.

When GCU applies JSON patches, it tries multiple orderings of patch operations to find one that passes YANG validation. During these intermediate attempts:
- PORT entries may temporarily be missing the required `lanes` field
- Tables like `PORT_QOS_MAP`, `QUEUE`, `BUFFER_PG` may reference ports that don't exist yet

Example errors:
```
ERR sonic_yang: Data Loading Failed:Missing required element "lanes" in "PORT_LIST"
ERR sonic_yang: Data Loading Failed:Invalid value "Ethernet0" in "ifname" element
ERR sonic_yang: Data Loading Failed:Leafref...points to a non-existing leaf
```

The `conftest.py` in `tests/generic_config_updater/` has an ignore pattern `".*ERR sonic_yang.*"` but it only applies to ONE host. The test's own `LOGANALYZER_IGNORE_REGEX` (which applies to ALL hosts via `ignore_expected_loganalyzer_errors` fixture) was missing this pattern.

#### How did you do it?

Added `".*ERR sonic_yang.*"` to `LOGANALYZER_IGNORE_REGEX` in `test_multiasic_addcluster.py`, which is applied to all DUT hosts via the `ignore_expected_loganalyzer_errors` fixture.

#### How did you verify/test it?

- Verified the error pattern matches the observed syslog entries
- Confirmed the fixture applies ignore patterns to all hosts in `duthosts`
- Cross-referenced with existing ignore pattern in `conftest.py` (line 93)

#### Any platform specific information?

N/A - applies to all multi-ASIC platforms running GCU operations.

#### Supported testbed topology if it's a new test case?

N/A - this is an improvement to an existing t2 topology test.

### Documentation

N/A - no new features or test cases added.

body:
- Addressed dependabot PR https://github.com/ably/ably-cli/pull/231
- Dependabot doesn't have permission to run E2E tests as per https://ably.atlassian.net/browse/DX-1017?focusedCommentId=89847

## Summary

- Upgrade `react` and `react-dom` from `^18.3.1` to `^19.2.4` across root, `packages/react-web-cli`, and `examples/web-cli`
- Upgrade `@types/react` from `^18.3.x` to `^19.2.14` and `@types/react-dom` from `^18.3.x` to `^19.2.3`
- Migrate `AblyCliTerminal` component away from `forwardRef` — `ref` is now a regular prop in React 19
- Fix `useRef` calls to pass required initial arguments (React 19 TypeScript requirement)
- Normalize `FitAddon` refs from `undefined` to `null` for consistency with all other refs in the file

## Why React 19

React 19 is the current stable release and brings significant improvements:

- **React Compiler support** — React 19 unlocks the [React Compiler](https://react.dev/learn/react-compiler), which can improve performance by **15–30%** by automating manual memoization (`useMemo`, `useCallback`). This means less boilerplate and fewer perf bugs.
- **`ref` as a regular prop** — No more `forwardRef` wrapper. Components accept `ref` directly, reducing indirection and making code simpler.
- **`use()` API** — Read promises and context directly in render, with conditional calling support (unlike hooks).
- **Actions & form handling** — `useActionState`, `useOptimistic`, `useFormStatus`, and `<form action={fn}>` simplify async state management and form handling with built-in pending states.
- **Document metadata** — `<title>`, `<meta>`, `<link>` rendered anywhere in the component tree are automatically hoisted to `<head>`.
- **Ref cleanup functions** — Ref callbacks can return a cleanup function, matching the `useEffect` pattern.
- **Better error handling** — New `onUncaughtError` and `onCaughtError` callbacks on `createRoot` for fine-grained error control.
- **Improved hydration** — Hydration error diffs show exactly what mismatched, making SSR debugging much easier.
- **Stylesheet management** — React automatically handles stylesheet insertion ordering for Suspense boundaries.
- **Custom Elements** — Full Web Components interop (passes all Custom Elements Everywhere tests).

## What was migrated

| Pattern | Before (React 18) | After (React 19) |
|---------|-------------------|-------------------|
| `forwardRef` wrapper | `forwardRef<Handle, Props>(InnerComponent)` | `ref` added to props interface, component accepts it directly |
| `useRef` without arg | `useRef<FitAddon>()` | `useRef<FitAddon \| null>(null)` |
| FitAddon ref reset | `secondaryFitAddon.current = undefined` | `secondaryFitAddon.current = null` |

## What didn't need changing

- `main.tsx` already used `createRoot` (no legacy `ReactDOM.render`)
- No `react-dom/test-utils` imports (tests use `@testing-library/react`)
- No string refs, `propTypes`, `defaultProps`, or legacy context patterns
- Peer dependencies `>=17.0.0` already covers React 19
- `React.FC` usage is fine (components don't rely on implicit `children`)

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm prepare` — builds successfully
- [x] `pnpm exec eslint .` — 0 errors
- [x] `pnpm test:unit` — 170 passed, 1 skipped (pre-existing)
- [x] `react-web-cli` package build — ESM + CJS + DTS all succeed
- [x] `react-web-cli` tests — 55 passed, 6 skipped (2 pre-existing failures unrelated to this change)
- [x] TypeScript compilation — 0 new errors (25 pre-existing in test file, same on `main`)
- [ ] Verify web-cli example app works in browser
- [ ] E2E tests pass in CI

author: brianmwas
body:
## What
- Make `KoogComposeContext` generic over app state type `S`
- Replace `KoogStateStore<*>` star projection with fully typed `KoogStateStore<S>`
- Add `initialState { }` DSL block as the entry point for typed state
- Wire `GuardrailEnforcer` into all tool calls via `GuardedTool` wrapper
- Fix CMP incompatibility: replace `System.currentTimeMillis()` with `Clock.System.now().toEpochMilliseconds()`
- Drop `data class` + `@ConsistentCopyVisibility` conflict in favour of plain class with manual `copy()`
- Remove dead code: `Phase.toKoogAgent`, `RetrieveFactsHistoryCompressionStrategy`, `updateHistory`
- Fix `CompressionTrigger.WithinPhase` reference → `AfterMessages`
- Update README to reflect generic DSL, `StatefulTool<S>`, and guardrails config

## Why
`KoogStateStore<*>` forced unsafe casts anywhere state was consumed. The star projection was a type hole — tools had no compile-time guarantee they were reading/writing the right state shape.

## Breaking changes
- `KoogComposeContext` constructor is now `KoogComposeContext<S>` — callers must either add a type param or use the stateless `koogCompose { }` overload which defaults to `Unit`
- `state()` builder method replaced by `initialState { }`

[opt] Use ReachableFrom rather than TransitiveClosure

This change introduces the ReachableFrom functions, which compute the set of nodes reachable from a given set of starting nodes in a directed graph. We support both adjacency lists & dense graphs represented using InlineBitmaps.

The register cleanup pass and proc state optimization pass are updated to use these new functions, replacing manual worklist implementations or less efficient transitive closure computations (O(N^3) vs. O(N+E)).

author: tuvshuutns
body:
## Summary

Reviewing the local changes since `origin/main`, I found two regressions that should be fixed before these changes are pushed.

## Findings

### 1. High: session integrity can silently disable itself on 4xx responses

The mobile client now treats `400/401/403/404` from `/session-integrity` as `skipped`, and then stops heartbeats entirely.

Relevant code:
- `mobileAppFrontend/src/security/session-integrity.ts`
- `cold-king-fc65/src/index.ts`

Details:
- In `mobileAppFrontend/src/security/session-integrity.ts`, non-OK responses that match `isPermanentSessionError()` return `skipped`.
- `heartbeat()` clears the timer and sets `stopped = true` when it sees `skipped`.
- `start()` also exits early on `skipped`.
- At the same time, the backend now explicitly returns `403` when the student profile cannot be resolved and `404` when the exam mapping cannot be resolved.

Why this is a bug:
- A stale announced-exam id, profile mismatch, or backend data inconsistency now turns off single-device session protection for the rest of the exam attempt.
- This fails open instead of failing closed or degrading to offline queueing.
- The user can continue the exam while session replacement detection is no longer running.

Suggested fix:
- Do not permanently stop heartbeats on these responses.
- Either keep queueing and retrying, or block exam start with a visible error instead of silently disabling integrity.

### 2. Medium: the take-exam screen no longer shows the exam title

Relevant code:
- `mobileAppFrontend/app/(student)/exam/[examId]/take.tsx`

Details:
- The redesigned take screen now renders only the subject label in the header.
- The previous `exam.title` block was removed and is no longer shown anywhere on the screen.

Why this is a bug:
- If a student has multiple active exams under the same subject, they cannot verify which exact exam they are currently taking after entering the attempt screen.
- This is a UX regression from the previous implementation, which clearly showed the exam title.

Suggested fix:
- Render `exam.title` again near the header or at the top of the scroll content.

## Summary

Replaces the bespoke `StatefulL2Executor` inside `ActionEngineClient` with the real `OpPayloadBuilder` stack. `L2Sequencer` now uses the production `L1OriginSelector` and `StatefulAttributesBuilder` to produce payload attributes, then delegates block building to `ActionEngineClient` via `start_build_block` / `get_sealed_payload` / `insert_unsafe_payload`. # Description

Fix tokenizer loading for forward pass logit check. b/497054985

- Previous behavior: if `test_args.hf_model_path` is local, load from `config.tokenizer_path`.
- This requires config.tokenizer_path to be huggingface format. Or would cause error, e.g.,
```
python3 -m tests.utils.forward_pass_logit_checker /deps/src/maxtext/configs//base.yml tokenizer_path=/deps/src/maxtext/assets/tokenizer.gemma3 load_parameters_path=gs://maxtext-gemma/unified/gemma3/4b/unscanned/2025-08-05-18-18/0/items model_name=gemma3-4b use_multimodal=false scan_layers=false --hf_model_path=./tmp/hf/gemma3-4b/2026-03-27-11-42 --max_kl_div=0.015 --run_hf_model=true

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(tokenizer_path, token=hf_token)
huggingface_hub.errors.HFValidationError: Repo id must be in the form 'repo_name' or 'namespace/repo_name': '/deps/src/maxtext/assets/tokenizers/tokenizer.gemma3'. Use `repo_type` argument if needed.
```
- Current behavior: 
  - (1) try load from `test_args.hf_model_path` first (eliminate the need of manually set config.tokenizer_path), 
  - (2) if error, fallback to `config.tokenizer_path` (e.g., dequantized hf checkpoint may not include tokenizer like gpt-oss)

Case 1: load from `test_args.hf_model_path`
```

--run_hf_model=true --hf_model_path=$HF_PATH \
tokenizer_path=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite tokenizer_type=huggingface
```

body:
## Summary
Fix the Windows CI OpenSC portable fallback filename interpolation bug.

## Root cause
The OpenSC portable fallback used strings like `OpenSC-$Version_x64.zip`, which PowerShell interpreted as the unset variable `$Version_x64` instead of `${Version}` plus the suffix.

## Fix
- use `${Version}` interpolation explicitly for portable OpenSC asset names

## Validation
- direct review against the latest failing CI log
- GitHub CI rerun after merge

## Summary
Refactored the locked transmitter equipment card layout from a horizontal flex layout to a vertical card design with improved visual hierarchy and usability.

## Key Changes
- **New component structure**: Created dedicated `transmitterCard`, `transmitterHeader`, and `transmitterBody` CSS classes to replace the generic `equipCardWide` styling
- **Layout redesign**: Changed from horizontal flex layout to vertical stacked layout with:
  - Centered header section containing icon and name
  - Body section with quantity controls, description, and minimum requirement text

- **Visual improvements**:
  - Added `minimumText` class for styled "Required minimum of 1" label
  - Centered alignment for header elements
  - Better spacing and visual separation between sections
- **Conditional rendering**: Added early return in `EquipCard` component to render locked wide cards with the new layout structure

## Implementation Details
- The refactored layout only applies to locked transmitter cards (`wide && locked` condition)
- Quantity controls are now contained in a bordered `quantityRow` with proper flex alignment
- The new CSS classes provide better semantic naming and clearer separation of concerns
- Removed the `equipCardWide` class entirely in favor of more specific component-based styling

author: copilot
body:
The `command: postgres -c unix_socket_directories=''` setting was passed through to the Docker entrypoint's temporary init server, which also sets `listen_addresses=''`. With no TCP and no Unix sockets, the init server was unreachable — `POSTGRES_DB` was never created. Because `initdb` had already written `PGDATA`, every subsequent restart skipped init entirely.

## Changes

- **`docker-compose.yml`**: Change `unix_socket_directories=''` → `unix_socket_directories='/tmp'`
  - `/tmp` is world-writable; the init temp server can create its socket there and complete `POSTGRES_DB` creation
  - `/var/run/postgresql` (root-owned on Proxmox) is still never touched
  - Backend connects via TCP so runtime socket location is irrelevant

- **`scripts/proxmox-setup.sh`**: Add a recovery step after `pg_isready` that checks whether the target database exists and creates it if missing — repairs systems that already ran the broken version with a stale `pgdata` volume

```yaml
# before
command: postgres -c unix_socket_directories=''

# after
command: postgres -c unix_socket_directories='/tmp'
```

body:
This pull request refactors the frontend and dashboard codebases to enable better code sharing and UI consistency by introducing a shared package and utilizing reusable UI components. It also improves playback queue handling, especially for shuffle mode, ensuring consistent queue order across client and server. Several files are updated to use the new shared utilities and UI components, and some redundant or duplicate code is removed.

Key changes include:

**Shared Packages and UI Component Adoption**
- Added the `packages/` directory to the Docker build context, enabling access to shared code and UI components across projects.
- Updated Vite config in `dashboard` to alias `@pneuma/shared` and `@pneuma/ui` for easier imports of shared utilities and UI components.
- Refactored `dashboard/src/main.ts` to import global styles from `@pneuma/shared/style.css` instead of a local file.
- Removed the local `dashboard/src/style.css` in favor of shared styles.
- Updated several frontend components (`Sidebar.svelte`, `Toasts.svelte`) to use shared UI components (`Sidebar`, `Toasts`) from `@pneuma/ui`, simplifying code and ensuring a consistent look and feel. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-8d75498df4d71ce3a9d36db08e7dd14e1b23ad77602c2c5b16789073975131dbR2-R79) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-c277b3114a9394255c500e4a503aa9855d95a8a7739e1b5541718d8ae9365127L2-R5)

**Frontend Codebase Refactoring and Shared Utilities**
- Replaced local utility imports (e.g., `shuffle`, `portal`, `totalDuration`) in frontend Svelte files with imports from `@pneuma/shared`, consolidating utility functions and reducing code duplication. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-20deba1536ce27f3164518a1314ab422e443be22dace612f6778a7dbed295bb8L29-R29) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-20deba1536ce27f3164518a1314ab422e443be22dace612f6778a7dbed295bb8L62-R62) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-8aa0138b8fb37e3e3e9a2afed2a189e4a5afadf19d693dffff81b260797e7b0eL15-R15)
- Updated `package.json.md5` to reflect changes in dependencies.

**Playback Queue and Shuffle Logic Improvements**
- Improved shuffle logic in `Library.svelte` and `Player.svelte` to always pin the selected track at the start of the queue and shuffle the rest, both for local and remote playback. The shuffled queue is now sent to the server to ensure client and server stay in sync, avoiding double-shuffling. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-20deba1536ce27f3164518a1314ab422e443be22dace612f6778a7dbed295bb8L359-R400) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-8aa0138b8fb37e3e3e9a2afed2a189e4a5afadf19d693dffff81b260797e7b0eL311-R352)
- When shuffle is toggled off, the original queue order is restored and sent to the server, maintaining accurate playback state.

**Component Interface and Prop Improvements**
- Updated several components (`TrackRow`, `Playlists.svelte`) to include a `disableLocal` prop, improving flexibility and clarity in component usage. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-20deba1536ce27f3164518a1314ab422e443be22dace612f6778a7dbed295bb8R638) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-9aed2396cebbce28af8e6549ce8597be7d15373e0c15d5a69086db8a8a68d076R382)

author: nuglifeleoji
body:
Fixes #2879.

## Problem

The `typing.cast("Schema", self.nested)` in `Nested.schema` was too
aggressive: it told mypy that `nested` is always a `Schema` instance.
This made the subsequent `isinstance(nested, Schema)` check always
evaluate to `True`, rendering the `else` branch — which handles string
and class references — unreachable according to mypy:

```
src/marshmallow/fields.py:627: error: Statement is unreachable  [unreachable]
```

PR #2878 worked around the issue by disabling `warn_unreachable`, but
left the underlying type-annotation inaccuracy unresolved.

## Fix

1. **Move the deferred `Schema` import** to the top of the `if not
   self._schema` block so the local `Schema` name is available when
   annotating `nested`.
2. **Annotate `nested` explicitly** as
   `Schema | SchemaMeta | str | dict[str, Field]`, which accurately
   reflects all possible values and lets mypy understand the subsequent
   isinstance checks.
3. **Update the `typing.cast`** to the same accurate union type.
4. **Simplify `isinstance(nested, (str, bytes))`** to
   `isinstance(nested, str)` — `bytes` was never part of the `nested`
   type annotation and `class_registry.get_class` only accepts `str`.
5. **Re-enable `warn_unreachable = true`** in `pyproject.toml`.

All existing tests pass and `mypy src/marshmallow/ --warn-unreachable`
reports no errors.

## Summary

Fixes CLA check failures on automated PRs from bot accounts (e.g. dependabot, renovate).

The existing `allowlist` field in the CLA assistant action was not matching bot authors correctly, causing PRs like #3009 to fail the CLA check. This adds an explicit bot detection step that:

1. Checks if the PR author's login ends with `[bot]`
2. Sets a success commit status for `CLAAssistant` when a bot is detected
3. Skips the CLA assistant action entirely via an additional `if` condition

This is in addition to the existing org membership skip and the CLA assistant's own allowlist, providing a reliable fallback.

### Motivation
- Provide Phase 5 clustering so faces with saved embeddings can be grouped into person clusters for review. 
- Expose Phase 6 read endpoints so the frontend can list jobs, browse person clusters, inspect cluster details and fetch thumbnails/previews.

### Description

This pull request introduces major improvements to the transaction system by adding unique, non-guessable transaction references and detailed sender/recipient account information to all transactions. It also ensures that transaction history responses expose these new fields in a consistent, public-facing format. The changes include new database migrations, model logic, and controller updates to support these enhancements.

**Database schema and data migration:**

* Added a new `transaction_reference` column to the `transactions` table, ensured uniqueness, and backfilled all existing transactions with ULID-based references for secure, non-sequential identification. (`database/migrations/2026_04_01_180000_add_transaction_reference_to_transactions_table.php`)
* Added new columns for `sender_account_name`, `sender_account_number`, `recipient_account_name`, and `recipient_account_number` to the `transactions` table. All existing transactions are backfilled with best-effort logic to populate these fields based on transaction type and available user/beneficiary data. (`database/migrations/2026_04_01_190000_add_sender_recipient_account_details_to_transactions_table.php`)

**Model logic enhancements:**

* Updated the `Transaction` model to automatically generate a unique `transaction_reference` ULID for every new transaction. Also added the new sender/recipient fields to the `$fillable` array. (`app/Models/Transaction.php`)

**API and controller improvements:**

author: soscpd
body:
## Summary

Implements client-side handling of the MCP `notifications/tools/list_changed`
notification (MCP spec §Tools). When any connected MCP server sends this
notification, nanobot re-enumerates tools from all connected servers and
refreshes the live tool registry without restarting.

## Motivation

Enables integration with dynamic MCP aggregators that act as a single
endpoint in front of a fleet of services. When the aggregator's service
list changes, it sends this notification and nanobot picks up the new
tools on the next agent turn.

## Behaviour

- Notification received → `tools/list` called on all connected servers
- Tool registry rebuilt from combined results
- No reconnection, no restart, no session interruption
- Compliant with MCP spec 2024-11-05+

## Changes

- **`nanobot/agent/tools/mcp.py`**: Extracted `_register_server_tools()` helper; added `refresh_mcp_tools()` and `setup_tools_list_changed_handler()`; `connect_mcp_servers()` now returns session map and wires up notification handlers
- **`nanobot/agent/tools/registry.py`**: Added `unregister_by_prefix()` for bulk MCP tool removal before re-registration
- **`nanobot/agent/loop.py`**: Stores returned sessions in `_mcp_sessions`

## Testing

- `test_tools_list_changed_triggers_refresh` — notification on one server calls `list_tools` on ALL servers
- `test_tools_list_changed_registry_reflects_updated_tools` — old tools removed, new tools present after notification
- `test_tools_list_changed_does_not_interrupt_sessions` — mid-flight tool execution completes normally during refresh

## Related

author: soscpd
body:
## Summary

Adds `security.ssrfAllowedSubnets` to config, allowing operators to
specify CIDR ranges that bypass the SSRF private-network guard.

## Motivation

Air-gapped and internal-only deployments need to reach services on RFC
1918 ranges. Per-hostname allowlisting is insufficient for volatile cluster
environments where hostnames vary per deployment. A CIDR allowlist is
deployment-stable.

## Config

```json
{
  "security": {
    "ssrfAllowedSubnets": ["172.16.0.0/12"]
  }
}
```

Default: `[]` — no change to existing behaviour.

## Security properties

- Default is unchanged: all private IPs are blocked unless explicitly listed
- Loopback and link-local remain blocked regardless of config
- CIDR validation happens at startup; invalid entries fail loudly
- Check occurs post-DNS-resolution to prevent rebinding bypasses

## Changes

- **`nanobot/config/schema.py`**: Added `SecurityConfig` with `ssrf_allowed_subnets` field
- **`nanobot/security/network.py`**: Added `_ALWAYS_BLOCKED`, `configure_allowed_subnets()`, updated `_is_private()` to check allowlist
- **`nanobot/config/loader.py`**: Calls `configure_allowed_subnets()` after loading config

## Testing

- `test_allowed_subnet_bypasses_private_block` — IP in allowed subnet passes
- `test_private_ip_not_in_allowlist_still_blocked` — uncovered private IP blocked
- `test_empty_allowlist_blocks_all_private` — default behaviour unchanged
- `test_invalid_cidr_raises_error` — bad CIDR fails at config time
- `test_loopback_blocked_even_if_allowlisted` — 127.x always blocked
- `test_multiple_subnets_configured` — multiple CIDR ranges work
- `test_link_local_blocked_even_if_allowlisted` — 169.254.x always blocked

## Summary

- **Remove `agents` and `commands` from plugin.json** — these aren't valid plugin manifest fields. Claude Code auto-discovers `agents/` and `commands/` directories. The `agents` field caused `claude plugin install qa-skills@neonwatty-qa` to fail with `agents: Invalid input`. No reference plugin (pr-review-toolkit, superpowers, commit-commands) declares these fields.
- **Remove `model` and `color` from agent frontmatter** — not used by any reference plugin's agents; dead weight.
- **Add `claude plugin validate .claude-plugin/plugin.json` to CI** — the root cause of this escaping: CI only ran `claude plugin validate .` which validates `marketplace.json`, not `plugin.json`. Now both manifests are schema-validated on every PR.

## Why CI missed this

`claude plugin validate .` validates the **marketplace** manifest (`marketplace.json`). `claude plugin validate .claude-plugin/plugin.json` validates the **plugin** manifest (`plugin.json`). CI only ran the first — so invalid fields in `plugin.json` were never caught. The JSON syntax check (`python3 -m json.tool`) confirmed valid JSON but not valid schema.

## Test plan

- [x] `claude plugin validate .claude-plugin/plugin.json` passes locally (was failing before)
- [x] `claude plugin validate .` passes locally
- [x] `npm run validate:skills` passes locally

author: besaleli
body:
Addresses feedback that getting started with `EncoderfileBuilder` requires too many imports — at minimum `EncoderfileBuilder`, `ModelType`, and often `TokenizerBuildConfig`, `BatchLongest` or `Fixed` depending on the use case.

Rather than flattening `EncoderfileBuilder` itself — which would have been a larger lift on the PyO3 side and would have cost us the type safety that makes the class useful for power users — we instead expose two convenience functions at the top level of the package:

- `encoderfile.build(...)` — builds an encoderfile binary from explicit configuration, with a flat argument structure that accepts primitives in place of supporting classes (e.g. `"sequence_classification"` instead of `ModelType.SequenceClassification`, `"batch_longest"` or an `int` instead of `BatchLongest()` / `Fixed(n=...)`). Tokenizer settings are flattened into `tokenizer_*` prefixed arguments, removing the need to import `TokenizerBuildConfig` for the common case.
- `encoderfile.build_from_config(...)` — thin wrapper around `EncoderfileBuilder.from_config()` for the common case where build settings are defined in a YAML file.

`EncoderfileBuilder` remains fully available for users who want the typed interface or finer control over the build process.

Also adds support for reading a Lua transform from a file path via `transform_path`, which was not previously possible without reading the file manually before passing it to the builder.

body: The way that konflux/Buildkit works is that it tears down evrything between RUN commands. When bazel runs, it daemonizes and stashes a copy of /etc/resolve.conf in a tmp directory. author: efiten
body:
## Problem

Fixes #325. Removing all home steps and clicking "Reset my theme" did not restore them.

## Root cause

Two-part bug:

**1. `SITE_CONFIG.home` permanently mutated at page load**
`app.js` calls `mergeUserHomeConfig(SITE_CONFIG, userTheme)` which does `SITE_CONFIG.home = Object.assign({}, serverHome, userTheme.home)`. If the user had `steps: []` saved in localStorage, this sets `SITE_CONFIG.home.steps = []` globally — permanently for the lifetime of the page.

**2. `initState()` reads the contaminated config**
When the customizer opens (or Reset is clicked), `initState()` reads `cfg = window.SITE_CONFIG`. Since `SITE_CONFIG.home.steps` is already `[]`, `state.home.steps` stays `[]` even after `localStorage.removeItem`. `autoSave()` then re-saves `steps: []` straight back.

**Secondary issue:** `data-rm-step` / add / move handlers didn't call `autoSave()`, making step persistence non-deterministic (only saved if a text field edit happened to be pending).

## Fix

- **`app.js`**: snapshot `SITE_CONFIG.home` before `mergeUserHomeConfig` → `window._SITE_CONFIG_ORIGINAL_HOME`
- **`customize.js`**: `initState()` uses `_SITE_CONFIG_ORIGINAL_HOME` instead of the contaminated `cfg.home`
- **`customize.js`**: add `autoSave()` to rm/move/add handlers for steps, checklist, and footer links

## Tests

2 new unit tests covering the snapshot bypass and DEFAULTS fallback. 231 tests pass.

## Checklist
- [x] Branches from `upstream/master`
- [x] No Matomo or local-only commits
- [x] Cache busters bumped
- [x] 231 tests pass, 0 fail

## Summary
- Adds dedup logic in `ChannelManager._dispatch_outbound()` — the single chokepoint for all outgoing messages
- Tracks recent messages by `(channel, chat_id, content_hash)` and suppresses identical messages sent more than 2 times within a 5-minute window

- Prevents agent loops from spamming users regardless of the underlying root cause

## Motivation
Guest agent was spamming guests with "I'm checking for any updates from Ebby!" every 5 minutes due to a `restrictToWorkspace` bug. While the root cause is fixed (PR #12), this guard provides defense-in-depth against any future agent loop scenarios.

## Summary

⚠️ Forked from https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19750 so will need to wait for that to be merged first

Moves `ConditionalDeployer` and `L2DevFeatureFlags` predeploy addresses down by one slot to close the gap left by the `FeeSplitter` removal in https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19750.

  ## Changes

  - `ConditionalDeployer`: `0x42...2C` → `0x42...2B`
  - `L2DevFeatureFlags`: `0x42...2D` → `0x42...2C`

  Updated in `Predeploys.sol`, `L2Genesis.s.sol`, `ConditionalDeployer.sol` and  `L2DevFeatureFlags.sol` predeploy annotations, the NUT bundle check script, semver-lock, upgrade bundle snapshot, and one op-deployer integration test.

  ## Motivation

  After removing the FeeSplitter predeploy at `0x42...2B`, the two subsequent predeploys had a gap in the address sequence. Since `FeeSplitter` `ConditionalDeployer` and `L2DevFeatureFlags` have not been deployed yet, we can still shift them down to keep the predeploy table contiguous.

## Proposed change

The `async_get_system_info` helper always loads the `hassio` component without consideration for whether Supervisor is in use in this system or not. This can create a secret dependency on the component and the `aiohasupervisor` library it uses. Most notably, bootstrap calls this helper in order to get various environment and system info cached:
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/f74256db2da4a16486f1ad1331ebe4779ebc86f5/homeassistant/bootstrap.py#L486

This breaks on installations without Supervisor as shown in #166976 .

Normally we use the `is_hassio` helper  that checks if the `hassio` component has been loaded combined with a local import to solve this. This seems problematic because this early in bootstrap the `hassio` component has not been loaded, nothing has. However `hassio` is only needed to enrich the response of this helper and bootstrap tosses the entire response without caching it. So its still safe to use this pattern here, we aren't losing anything needed during bootstrap.

There's a short discussion [here](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/166976#issuecomment-4172668734) and [in discord](https://discord.com/channels/330944238910963714/1488952602380075179/1488952650258190539) on some possible better alternative solutions that don't cause `aiohasupervisor` to be installed almost always even when there's no Supervisor. However this PR is takes the simplest fix so it can be safely included in current release, improved fixes can be tackled separately later if we wish.

### ⚠️ WORK IN PROGRESS - DO NOT MERGE
This PR is currently under development and is not yet ready for merging. The following items must be addressed:

1. We need to establish a definitive method for determining if two policies are identical. The upstream **Pydantic model fields** are not yet finalized. Implementing identity logic now would be premature; we will revisit this once the schema is stable.
2. Currently, the implementation treats **Segments** and **Zones** as interchangeable. We need to refactor the logic to group consecutive curb segments with the same policies into curb zone.

----------------------------------------------------------------------

This pull request introduces a modular pipeline for processing curb policy updates, extracting data from staging database, transforming it into a set of normalized tables, and exporting the results as CSV files which will be later loaded into the api database. The changes add new modules for extraction, transformation, and export, and orchestrate them through a new pipeline entrypoint. The most important changes are grouped below:

**Pipeline Orchestration and Entry Point**

* Added `pipeline.py` to orchestrate the full process: loading environment variables, extracting data, transforming it, and exporting the results. Includes a CLI interface for specifying a job ID and robust logging throughout the process.

**Data Extraction**

* Added `extractor.py` with the `read_db_tables` function to connect to the database, retrieve specified tables from a schema, and handle errors with logging.

**Data Transformation**

* Added `transformer.py` to flatten and normalize the staging data into curb zones, policies, rules, time spans, and their relationships. The transformation includes deduplication of policies using hashing, memory management, and conversion to DataFrames.

**Data Export**

* Added `exporter.py` to export processed DataFrames to CSV files in a specified directory, with logging and error handling for empty or invalid data.

author: mattkram
body: ## Summary This is a POC, heavily inspired by the approach used in https://github.com/jezdez/conda-express, to bootstrap a standalone environment containing the Anaconda CLI (implemented in Python). In order to do this, we statically embed a cross-platform lockfile and install using `rattler`. When the user runs the bootstrap command, they get our CLI packages, plus a Python runtime, isolated from all other system conda/python environments. At this point, we are doing this for a few reasons: * To better understand the underlying technology to understand edges and learn * To prototype a method for rapidly shipping existing CLI functionality, all bootstrapped from `ana`, without having to do a full rewrite * As a foundation for a **possible** general mechanism for tool installation ### How it works * Adds a new subcommand `ana bootstrap`, which invokes the bootstrapping process * There is a step included as well to do this in the `install.sh` script, after the `ana` binary is installed * We store a rattler v6 lockfile, which is statically compiled into `ana` at build time. This could be extended in the future to fetch a package spec from a service for things like custom tools, etc. * We use `rattler` to install a new environment inside `~/.ana/tools/anaconda-cli` * We symlink the binary into `~/.ana/bin`. This is configurable per-tool, in cases where multiple entrypoints might need to be exposed (inside `lockfiles.rs`) * The `~/.ana/bin` directory is also put onto `PATH` inside the `install.sh` script * Adds a simple `ana org ...` wrapper, which runs `anaconda org ...` in a subprocess. This is just to demonstrate what a subprocess-level wrapper might look like ### Some design details * The lockfile is configured specifically to use https://repo.anaconda.com (as opposed to conda-forge). We add `anaconda-cloud` channel on anaconda.org just because some of the packages are not in main yet * One reason to pursue this approach is we can configure where the packages for the tool environments come from. In the future, with some backend services, we can potentially make this dynamic based on user/customer preferences * We don't do any channel configuration yet The binary size is now 15MB, compared to ~10MB of the current `main` branch build. Primary size increase is the one time addition of the rattler crates. Preliminary testing shows addition of more lockfiles has negligible effect on the binary size. ### Benchmarking Preliminary benchmarking shows the bootstrapping process completing in <2s, with a cleared rattler cache: ### Known issues * On macOS, the first execution of `anaconda` is very slow. This is due to a combination of byte-compiling the Python code, but also most likely due to the Gatekeeper security feature of macOS, because it considers the entire folder as something that needs to be scanned. * This does not (yet) do any shell activation, to the same extent that `pixi run` and `pixi shell` do. For `anaconda` CLI packages this should be fine, but this needs to be solved more generically if we decide to extend this feature more generally. Jira: [CLI-377](https://anaconda.atlassian.net/browse/CLI-377) [CLI-377]: https://anaconda.atlassian.net/browse/CLI-377?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ

author: d1donlydfink
body:
@andreidenissov-cog is primary.

This PR is largely a refactor for clarification in many different places as to when resources are to be closed.

* Create the notion of a LingeringResource which distinguishes between the following periods of close() timing:
    * close_of_request() - This is what needs to happen when the request is done
    * close_of_work() - This is what needs to happen when the work of the request is done
    For chatbots, the timing of these are the same, but for events they are different.
    Both of these are asynchronous.
* Move a bunch of different kinds of object to inherit from this new LingeringResource interface:
    * InvocationContext
    * DataDrivenChatSession
    * RunContext
    * LangChainLlmResources
    * CallableActivation
    * FrontMan
    * ServiceAgentReservations 
    For the most part, anyone who had a delete_resources() has that method renamed to close_of_work() for clarity.
* Worth noting that we are _not_ converting LlmPolicy objects to LingeringResources just yet. They also have a delete_resources() method, but they are also potentially externally derived from for folks' pet LLMs. So don't mess with that.
* Do not close() the reservationist or sly_data in DataDrivenChatSession.finalize_run() any more. Do that in close_of_work()  - This was one of the main separations that needed to happen to get manual events to work
* Separate previous SessionInvocationContext.close() into 2 phases:
    * close_of_request() closes the message queue
    * close_of_work() moves the AsyncioExecutor back into the pool
* Now that InvocationContext.close() is asynchronous from the LingeringResource interface, some work to run close() in an executor from the Sessions is done.

What's nice about these changes is that:
* It clarifies when things get closed (just a regular close() wouldn't tell you anything when looking at the code)
* It allows for me to manually test that events still work merely by commenting out the single call to close_of_work() in LingeringResource.close()

Manually tested:
* Regular requests still work
* Events still work when commenting out close_of_work() in LingeringResource.close().

Future work:
* Hand off event-based InvocationContexts (only) to a separate server thread for proper closure and Executor return to pool. (This will be what https://github.com/cognizant-ai-lab/neuro-san/issues/815 is about)
* Figure out close_of_work() semantics for external agent calls in that new world
* Figure out close and event semantics in a library/direct-session capacity.

author: rtollert
body:
### Summary of Changes

/var/local/natinst/log must be owned by lvuser:ni with mode 775; otherwise, NI software will fail to start. nisetupkernelconfig is failing to do this if it decides to mkdir it.

---

The known steps to reproduce this in an organic way are rather obscure but are known to be customer-visible.

1. [Create an RT System Image](https://www.ni.com/docs/en-US/bundle/ni-system-configuration-lv-ref/page/nisyscfg/create_system_image.html) while blacklisting the `/var/local/natinst/log` directory to ensure that existing logs are not stored in the image.
2. [Reformat the RT target](https://www.ni.com/docs/en-US/bundle/ni-system-configuration-lv-ref/page/nisyscfg/format_system.html). **Do not install a Base System Image (BSI).**
3. [Set the system image](https://www.ni.com/docs/en-US/bundle/ni-system-configuration-lv-ref/page/nisyscfg/set_system_image.html) back onto the reformatted target. Again, include `/var/local/natinst/log` in the blacklist. (I believe that if you don't install the BSI then it is not necessary to blacklist this on Set Image in order to reproduce this.)

The upshot is that the BSI is setting the right permissions on install, but system images skip that entirely. Normally `/var/local/natinst/log` is saved to a system image, with the right permissions. But if it's omitted then it will have whatever permissions safemode has set for it, which, thanks to this initscript, are incorrect.

### Justification

[AB#3808658](https://dev.azure.com/ni/DevCentral/_workitems/edit/3808658)

### Testing

None (trivial change)

* [ ] I have built the core package feed with this PR in place. (`bitbake packagefeed-ni-core`)

body:
## Description

Implements an end-to-end A2A agent card import flow: server-side validation and registration endpoints, a `TypedMetadata` polymorphic model persisted in the DB, and a multi-step registration modal in the web UI.

- Implements A2A agent card validation with spec version auto-detection (v0.3 / v1.0)
- Adds dedicated `POST /api/v1/catalog/register` endpoint — validates raw card, parses via A2A parser plugin (Product Archetype: raw card → CatalogEntry), persists the entry
- Adds `POST /api/v1/catalog/validate` dry-run endpoint (no persistence, returns structured errors + preview)
- Implements `TypedMetadata` polymorphic model for protocol-specific metadata (extensions, security schemes, interfaces, signatures); `CatalogEntry.MarshalJSON` now uses `MarshalTypedMetaJSON` so each `typed_meta` item includes a `"kind"` discriminator in API responses
- `SyncFromDB` handles `UnmarshalTypedMetaJSON` errors — defaults `TypedMeta` to an empty slice instead of silently dropping corrupted data
- Adds 4-step registration modal in the web UI (input → validation errors → preview → confirm)
- Wires all new endpoints under auth (`catalog:write` permission)
- Adds frontend unit tests (Vitest) and Go unit tests for all new handlers
- Adds `make check` target (fmt + vet + lint + web-lint) and `make web-test`
- Adds `test-frontend` job to CI; `build` now requires lint + test + test-frontend to pass
- Extracts shared `handleUnauthorized()` helper in `web/src/api.ts` — used by both `request()` and `validateAgentCard()` for consistent 401 handling and auth state cleanup
- Fixes `docs/api.md` and `README.md` examples: `protocol` is `"a2a"` (lowercase), `spec_version` is `"1.0"` (no `v` prefix), and `typed_meta` is documented as an array with kind-discriminated objects

# Pull Request

## Summary

Large UI/backend integration and baseline reset, including CI pipeline fixes and several code quality/correctness fixes applied from PR review feedback.

### Title
Large UI/Backend Integration/Baseline Reset

### Description

**What Changed:**
- Various UI and backend integration changes (baseline reset)
- **CI Fix** (`.github/workflows/ci-release-gate.yml`): The `e2e-workflow-gate` job was previously using `dotnet restore PTDoc.sln` and `dotnet build PTDoc.sln`, which includes `PTDoc.Maui` and requires MAUI workloads not available on the ubuntu CI runner. Replaced with project-specific restore/build commands (`src/PTDoc.Api/PTDoc.Api.csproj` and `tests/PTDoc.Tests/PTDoc.Tests.csproj`), consistent with all other gates in the same workflow.
- **Bash fix** (`cleanbuild-ptdoc.sh`): Fixed invalid arithmetic-expansion pipeline syntax for `CORE_PROJECT_REFS_COUNT`; replaced with correct command substitution `$(...)`.
- **Compliance fix** (`src/PTDoc.Application/Compliance/IRulesEngine.cs`): Removed CPT code `97150` (group therapy — billed per-encounter, not subject to the 8-minute rule) from `KnownTimedCptCodes.Codes` to prevent incorrect timed-unit validation.
- **Audit trail fix** (`src/PTDoc.Api/AI/AiEndpoints.cs`): All three AI audit-log `userId` lookups now prefer `PTDocClaimTypes.InternalUserId` and fall back to `ClaimTypes.NameIdentifier`, ensuring audit records consistently use PTDoc's internal user ID even for external auth flows.
- **Secret hygiene fix** (`src/PTDoc.Api/appsettings.Testing.json`): Replaced the API-key-shaped `AzureOpenAIKey` test value with a `REPLACE_WITH_TEST_AZURE_OPENAI_KEY` placeholder, keeping the repo's "no key-shaped values in tracked files" policy consistent.
- **Auth response fix** (`src/PTDoc.Api/Identity/AuthEndpoints.cs`): PIN-login `AccountLocked` and `PendingApproval` 403 responses now return structured `ProblemDetails` (with a `status` extension field) instead of anonymous objects, giving clients a consistent, well-typed response contract.

**Why:**
- The `e2e-workflow-gate` CI job was failing with `NETSDK1147: To build this project, the following workloads must be installed: maui-android` because the full solution restore pulled in the MAUI project on an ubuntu runner that lacks MAUI workloads.
- The bash pipeline bug in `cleanbuild-ptdoc.sh` would silently fail the architecture-validation step at runtime.
- `97150` is a group therapy code billed per-encounter, not per timed unit; including it in `KnownTimedCptCodes` caused false validation failures.
- Audit records in AI endpoints could reference an external identity subject (`oid`/`sub`) instead of the PTDoc internal user ID, making audit trails inconsistent.
- A test-only API-key-shaped string in a tracked file risks secret-scanner false positives and normalises putting key-shaped values in source control.
- Returning anonymous objects for 403 PIN-login errors forced clients to branch on both HTTP status and response shape.

**How:**
- Changed the restore and build steps in `e2e-workflow-gate` from full-solution commands to individual project commands. `PTDoc.Tests` does not reference `PTDoc.Maui`, so no E2E test coverage is lost.
- Fixed `CORE_PROJECT_REFS_COUNT` to use `$(grep ... | wc -l ...)` command substitution.
- Removed `"97150"` entry from `KnownTimedCptCodes.Codes`.
- Added `using PTDoc.Application.Identity;` to `AiEndpoints.cs` and updated all three `userId` lookups to `(httpContext.User.FindFirst(PTDocClaimTypes.InternalUserId) ?? httpContext.User.FindFirst(...NameIdentifier))?.Value`.
- Replaced `"test-api-key-for-integration-tests-only"` with `"REPLACE_WITH_TEST_AZURE_OPENAI_KEY"` in `appsettings.Testing.json`.
- Rewrote both 403 branches in `PinLogin` to construct and return `ProblemDetails` with `Extensions["status"]`.

author: xiaoxmeng
body:
Summary:

CONTEXT: The nimble serializer/deserializer needed several improvements:
(1) Stream sizes in the kCompactRaw trailer only supported Trivial and Varint
encoding. Stream sizes tend to be similar across streams, making delta encoding
a natural fit. However, in practice delta-varint provides marginal savings over
plain varint for stream sizes since the values vary enough that deltas don't
compress much better.
(2) DeserializerOptions required callers to pass a full SerializationVersion,
but the deserializer auto-detects version from the header byte — only a bool
flag is needed.
(3) StreamData took two separate bool flags (encodingEnabled, useVarintRowCount)
instead of deriving them from the version.
(4) Several helper functions were missing for version classification.

WHAT:
- Add Zigzag.h utility (branchless zigzag encode/decode for int32/int64) and
  Delta encoding support for kCompactRaw stream sizes. Delta encoding stores
  the first value as-is, then zigzag+varint encodes consecutive deltas.
  Wire: [0x08][count:varint][first:varint][zigzag(delta_1):varint]...[trailer_size:u32]

- Simplify DeserializerOptions: replace `std::optional<SerializationVersion> version`
  with `bool hasHeader`. When true, auto-detect version from the first byte of
  serialized data. When false, assume kLegacy (no version header).

- Simplify StreamData: take SerializationVersion instead of two bool flags
  (encodingEnabled, useVarintRowCount), derive both internally.

- Add version helper functions in Options.h:
  - `nonLegacyFormat()`: returns true for kCompact/kCompactRaw/kTabletRaw
  - `isRawFormat()`: returns true for kCompactRaw/kTabletRaw
  - `isTabletRawFormat()`: returns true for kTabletRaw only

- Add validation in Serializer constructor: reject explicit kLegacy and kTabletRaw
  versions, validate streamSizesEncodingType requires non-legacy version.

- Extract `StreamDataReader::readVersion()` method for version header parsing.

- Add fuzz tests for mixed-version serialization and projection (cycles through
  kCompact, kCompactRaw, kCompactRaw+Delta) with decode verification.

- SST writer benchmark: remove sst_partitioned_index flag, change
  nimble_stream_sizes_encoding default from Trivial to Delta.

Reviewed By: srsuryadev, jiahaol-work, tanjialiang

Differential Revision: D98941222

author: oceans404
body:
## Summary

Fixes the root cause of #450 and addresses #370 — when `stellar scaffold init` pulls OpenZeppelin example contracts, the project's `Cargo.toml` workspace dependencies are never updated to match the OZ version the CLI downloads. Additionally, `LATEST_SUPPORTED_OZ_RELEASE` pointed at an unaudited RC (`v0.7.0-rc.1`) that requires soroban-sdk 25.x, incompatible with the template's soroban-sdk 23.x.

### Change 1: Fix `get_workspace_root` path (the dep-update bug)

In `generate_oz_example`, `get_workspace_root` was called with the **cache** path (`~/.cache/stellar-scaffold-cli/openzeppelin-stellar-contracts/examples/...`). This means `cargo locate-project --workspace` found the cached OZ repo's workspace `Cargo.toml` — not the project's. So `update_workspace_dependencies` either modified the wrong file or failed silently, leaving the project pinned to whatever version the template shipped with.

**Fix:** Pass `dest_path` (the project's `contracts/<name>` directory) instead.

### Change 2: Use stable OZ v0.6.0 instead of v0.7.0-rc.1

`v0.7.0-rc.1` depends on `soroban-sdk 25.x`, which conflicts with the template's `soroban-sdk 23.x` and causes duplicate `panic_impl` lang item errors. `v0.6.0` is the latest stable release and works with `soroban-sdk ^23.4.0`.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo check` passes
- [x] Fresh `stellar scaffold init` correctly updates OZ dep tags from v0.5.1 → v0.6.0
- [x] Combined with companion PR (scaffold-stellar-frontend#190), `npm run dev` builds, deploys, and generates clients for all 3 example contracts with zero errors

Closes #450
Addresses #370

author: zeroshade
body:
## Summary

- Add support for binding `Timestamp`, `Binary`, `LargeBinary`, `Decimal128`, and `Decimal256` Arrow types as query parameters in `convertArrowToNamedValue`
- These types previously fell through to the `default` case and returned `StatusNotImplemented`
- The fix is entirely in the ADBC layer — gosnowflake already accepts `time.Time`, `[]byte`, and `string` via `database/sql`

## Type Mapping

| Arrow Type | Go Value | Wrapper |
|---|---|---|
| `Timestamp` (all units/timezones) | `time.Time` | `sql.NullTime` |
| `Binary` / `LargeBinary` | `[]byte` | `nil` for NULL |
| `Decimal128` / `Decimal256` | `string` (via `ToString(scale)`) | `sql.NullString` |

## Details

- **Timestamp**: Uses `arrow.TimestampType.GetToTimeFunc()` to correctly handle all time units (s/ms/µs/ns) and timezone conversion
- **Binary/LargeBinary**: Passed directly as `[]byte`; `nil` for NULL values (no `sql.NullBinary` equivalent exists)
- **Decimal128/Decimal256**: Formatted as strings using `Num.ToString(scale)` to preserve full precision — avoids float64 precision loss

## Testing

Added 16 unit tests covering:
- Each new type with valid values
- NULL handling for each type

### Motivation
- Introduce a clear internal distinction between active vs passive recovery so notifications reflect whether a channel improved because people engaged or simply went quiet.
- Keep notifications short and aligned with existing tone while making key words and timing more prominent with bold formatting.

### Description
- Added recovery classification in `_evaluate_barcello_channel(...)` by querying current and previous window message counts and computing `recovery_type = "active" | "passive"` via `
  _determine_barcello_recovery_type(...)`.
- Detection rules: `passive` when `message_count_current_window <= threshold_low_activity` (config `recovery.threshold_low_activity`, default `2`) or when `message_count_current_window < previous * 0.3`; otherwise `active`.
- Wired `recovery_type` into UX: introduced `_decorate_barcello_transition_message(...)` to produce concise recovery subtitles with bolded state (e.g. `**VERDE**`) and added active/passive emoji (`📈`/`🌿`).
- Reworked trend helper to `_render_barcello_trend_comment(state, delta_score, recovery_type)` with distinct second-bullet phrasing for `active` vs `passive` and ensured first trend bullet always bolds the elapsed time (e.g. `**7 minuti fa**`).
- Files changed: `app/services/triggers_service.py` (helpers + integration + formatting) and tests updated/added in `tests/test_barcello_event_driven.py` (dual-window count mocking and new assertions).

## Summary

Implements a production-grade RAG agent for book recommendations following Databricks best practices:

- **Retrieval**: Vector Search queries return top 3 matching book summaries
- **Generation**: LLM synthesizes structured recommendations grounded in actual summary text
- **Tracing**: Full MLflow observability with spans for retriever and LLM operations
- **Visualization**: LangGraph state machine with Mermaid diagram

## What changed

- **`notebooks/3_agent_with_vector_search.py`** — Complete RAG pipeline with:
  - Retrieval node querying VS index for top 3 matches
  - Generation node calling LLM with retrieved context
  - Structured JSON output: book title, reason, key insight
  - @mlflow.trace() decorators on retrieve_summaries() and generation_node()

author: andreykuzmin1994-blip
body:
## Summary
Implements automatic failover from Anthropic (Claude) to OpenAI with a circuit breaker pattern to keep the kiosk intake session alive during provider outages. This ensures applicants aren't blocked by temporary AI service disruptions.

## Key Changes

- **New `aiProvider.js` service**: Centralized AI provider abstraction with:
  - Automatic failover logic that routes to OpenAI if Anthropic fails
  - Circuit breaker implementation to prevent cascading failures
  - Provider-agnostic model tier routing (HAIKU/SONNET) that maps to the correct model for whichever provider is active
  - Intelligent error classification: fails over on service errors (5xx, timeouts, auth failures) but retries on client errors (400, 429)
  - Failover audit log (last 50 events) for operational visibility

- **Updated `aiAssistant.js`**: 
  - Refactored to use `aiProvider.sendMessage()` instead of direct Anthropic client calls
  - Changed `selectModel()` to return provider-agnostic tier names instead of model IDs
  - Now returns both `model` and `provider` in response for transparency

- **New health check endpoint** (`/api/health/ai`):
  - Reports active provider, circuit breaker state, and recent failover events
  - Useful for monitoring and debugging failover behavior

- **Configuration**:
  - Optional `OPENAI_API_KEY` environment variable enables failover
  - Tunable `AI_FAILOVER_THRESHOLD` (default: 3 consecutive failures) and `AI_FAILOVER_RESET_MS` (default: 60s)
  - Backward compatible: works with Anthropic-only setup if OpenAI key not provided

- **Comprehensive test coverage**: Unit tests for circuit breaker state transitions and failover error classification

## Implementation Details

- **Circuit breaker states**: CLOSED (normal) → OPEN (failing, reject requests) → HALF_OPEN (testing recovery)
- **Failover strategy**: Auth errors (401/403) trigger failover because applicants at the kiosk can't fix revoked keys; rate limits (429) don't failover since they're temporary
- **Message format conversion**: Transparently converts between Anthropic and OpenAI message formats
- **Session tracking**: Hashes session tokens for Anthropic metadata without exposing raw tokens
